did_you_know.text: Did you know? Esther entered the inner court of the royal palace wearing her royal robes, even though she had not been summoned to appear before the king.
Did you know? When the king saw Esther, she won his favor, and he extended the golden scepter toward her. Touching the tip of the scepter symbolized that he welcomed her.
Did you know? The king asked Esther twice what she wanted and offered her up to half the kingdom, using broad and emphatic language as a promise.
Did you know? Esther did not present her request immediately. Instead, she invited the king and Haman to a banquet she had prepared.
Did you know? Even after the king asked Esther at the banquet what her petition and request were, she invited him and Haman to another banquet the following day.
Did you know? Haman left the banquet happy and in high spirits, but when he saw Mordecai at the king’s gate, and Mordecai neither stood up nor moved for him, Haman was filled with rage.

Did you know? Haman boasted about his wealth, his sons, his honor, and his invitations to Esther’s banquets, but declared that none of it meant anything to him as long as he saw Mordecai sitting at the king’s gate.
Did you know? Zeresh and Haman’s friends suggested preparing a pole fifty cubits high and asking the king to have Mordecai impaled on it. Haman accepted their advice and prepared the pole.
